It is stated that major portion of the said khatian was hilly jungle land and a part of it including schedule-A was ballad; that aforesaid original owners used to possess the same by giving lease to tenants; that accordingly, out of schedule 'A' land, the aforesaid original owners leased out 0.140 sahasrangsha i.e. 7 gandas of land, as described in schedule 'B' to defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, on 19-7-1938 by acceptance of salami and rent and that the defendant No. 31 Khaled Solaiman used to possess the lease-hold land by cultivating it through abraders on payment of rent to the landlords and their transferees who recognized and admitted defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman as raiyat under them. It is further stated that subsequently, with the expansion of Chittagong town, habitation and construction of dwelling houses started in the surrounding land; that accordingly, the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, also constructed 2 kutcha dwelling houses in part of the schedule 'B' land which appertained to Municipal holding No. 150 and was possessing the same on payment of rents and taxes and thus the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, was in possession of the schedule 'B' land as tenant and by exercising his own right openly and adversely to other defendants for over statutory period of limitation; that while the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, was in khas possession of the entire schedule 'B' land, he sold 4 gandas equivalent to 0.80 sataks as described in schedule 'B'(1) together with the house appertaining to Municipal holding No. 150 to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 27th May, 1977 for valuable consideration and put the plaintiff in possession of the same. 

 5. It is further stated that Saleh Ahmed, predecessor of defendants Nos. 1 to 9 and 10 to 15, filed Title Suit No. 29 of 1959 in the court of the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong for declaration of tenancy khas dakhali right in 4 kanis of land out of which 19½ gandas in schedule 'A' and balance in RS plot Nos. 60 and 67 of khatian No. 246 on the allegation that the aforesaid owners granted 9 years' lease of 4 Kanis of land of RS plot Nos. 60, 66, 67 to one Pitambar; that Pitamber died leaving son Mukhia Jamadar and he was in possession of the same and while in possession he sold 4 kanis of land to Abdus Sobhan Chowdhury, predecessor or defendants Nos. 1 to 15 and put him in possession of the land except the land covered by a house in which the seller was in permissive possession for some time and that subsequently, Mukhia did not give possession of house and also denied their title and hence they filed the said suit. 

 18. Mr Omar Faruque, the learned Advocate for the respondents, submits that the land in schedule A together with other land of RS khatian No. 246 of mouza Lalkhan Bazar formerly PS Kotwali, at present PS Double Mooring, District Chittagong originally belonged to Sailendra Krishna, Pram Krishna and Gokul Krishna in 13½ annas share and Harendra Kumar in 2½ annas share; that accordingly, RS khatian was prepared and finally published in the name of aforesaid owners; that by amicable arrangement, Harendra Kumar surrendered his share in the land of said khatian in favour of Sailendra Krishna, Pram Krishna and Gokul Krishna and they were in possession of the same on payment of rent to the superior landlord and that the subsequently aforesaid owner transferred their interest in the suit khatian to their wives Mrs Lalita Roy, Purnarama Roy and Rajubala Roy respectively. He further submits their the original owners used to possess the same by giving lease to tenants; that accordingly out of schedule 'A' land, the aforesaid original owners leased out 0.140 sahasrangsha i.e. 7 gandas of land as described in schedule 'B' to defendant No. 31 Khaled Solaiman, that while the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, was in khas possession of the entire schedule 'B' land, he sold 4 gandas equivalent to 0.80 sataks as described in schedule B(1) together with the house appertaining to Municipal holding No. 150 to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 27th May, 1977 for valuable consideration and put the plaintiff in possession of the same. It is further submitted that after purchase the plaintiff constructed one more kutcha house on schedule B(1) land and repaired the previous houses and let out to 6 temporary tenants. The plaintiff Moulana Mohammad Harun-ur-Rashid has also undertaken construction of 4-storied building on part of schedule B(1) land and has completed construction of ground floor, safety tank and pucca boundary wall as per plan of CDA approved plan vide BC Case No. 467 of 1977 and installed WASA water lines and electric lines. It is further submitted that the defendants title in 19½ gandas in suit plot has been declared but in the aforesaid plot the total area of land is 41½ kanis which is much in excess of the land of the share of defendant Nos. 1 to 15; that the original, landlords before leasing out the land of Patambar, out of the suit plot No. 66 leased out 7½ gandas land to plaintiff's predecessor the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, as such there is no clash of title between the plaintiff and defendants No. 1 to 15 and other co-sharers and the same is required to be partitioned. Mr Faruque further submits that the impugned judgment and decree was legally passed which should not be interfered. 

 33. There, is another aspect of this appeal. The defendant-appellants claim right title and interest in 19½ gandas in suit RS plot No. 66 along with 3 kanis 1/2 gandas = 60½ gandas in non suited plot No. 60 and 67 measuring total area of 4 kanis land by registered kabala dated 8-8-1947 from the original owner and at one point of dispute the predecessor of the defendant-appellants constrained to bring title Suit No. 29 of 1959 [subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 17 of 1961 and Title Suit No. 12 of 1962] and after contested hearing appellants predecessor obtained decree on 10-9-1964 and during trial, the suit land was investigated by Mr Saleh Ahamed Chowdhury, the learned pleader Commissioner, whose investigation report, sketch map, field book etc. have been made part of the decree of the aforesaid suit. That 19½ gandas in eastern portion of suit schedule RS plot No. 66 was given to the appellants in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 29 of 1959 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 17 of 1961 and Title Suit No. 12 of 1962 shown in the trace map of the investigation report. Since the predecessors of the plaintiff-respondent were parties in that suit, so the plaintiff-respondent is bound by the decree of that suit. Thus the suit is barred by res judicata. The condition of res judicata is that former suit must have been a suit between the same parties or between the parties under whom they or any of them claim. This condition recognises the general principle of law that the judgment and decrees bind the parties and privies. Therefore, when it is admitted that the predecessors of the plaintiffs-respondents were the parties in Suit No. 29 of 1959 (previous No. 17 of 1961 and 12 of 1962), the judgment and decree of that suit bind the plaintiff-respondent and the present suit is barred by resjudicata. By dint of judgment and decree of aforesaid Title Suit No. 17 of 1961, the defendant-appellants put into Khas possession in maximum decretal land by the Court through execution case, but the present respondent No. 1 resisted the execution in 4 gandas by filing Title Suit No. 50 of 1978 as plaintiff in the First Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Sadar, Chittagong and his ex parte order of ad interim injunction was vacated after contested hearing by order No. 24 dated 31-7-1978 (Exhibit-Kha(1)) and the present respondent No. 1 voluntarily got the suit dismissed for default in his previous Title Suit No. 50 of 1978 by order dated 17-3-1986, but in the meantime, the respondent No.1 as plaintiff surreptitiously filed present Partition Suit No. 50 of 1979 renumbered as Partition Suit No. 409 of 1984 on 13-4-1979. The plaintiff- respondent No. 1 as his devised policy deviated from his earlier admission made in the plaint of Other Suit No. 50 of 1978 in the present suit and manufactured various forged, concocted, frivolous and fictitious documents in his favour. The learned court below arrived at erroneous finding and decision and thereby decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 31-8-1939.
